result.title: GeoFlip: Benchmarking Geometry-Sensitive Physics in Video Generation
result.summary: Video generation models synthesize realistic motion, but can they respond correctly to changes in initial geometry? We introduce GeoFlip, a video generation benchmark centered on physical outcome flips induced by geometry. With shared physical settings and textual prompts held fixed, GeoFlip applies controlled interventions to support extent, object placement, and mechanism configuration, constructing paired scenes with contrasting reference events, such as remaining stable versus falling or tipping. These pairs test whether models translate geometric differences in the first frame into correct physical evolution. The benchmark comprises 482 scene pairs and 964 reference videos across six physical categories, with reference outcomes established through procedural scene construction, physics simulation, and numerical validation and verification of physical events. We evaluate 16 models for image to video generation along three dimensions: event correctness, structural integrity, and similarity to reference videos. We examine evaluation consistency with independent vision language judges. On the 442 conditions shared by all models, the highest event correctness averaged across tasks is 27.98%, revealing substantial limitations in physical generation conditioned on geometry. Model strengths vary across physical mechanisms, and the three evaluation dimensions capture distinct capabilities. Typical failures include ignoring geometric changes, generating incorrect object motion, bending rigid objects, and introducing additional components. Rank correlations between judges reach 0.906 for event correctness and 0.929 for structural integrity. By combining controlled geometric interventions, verifiable physical references, and multidimensional evaluation, GeoFlip assesses progress from visual realism toward physical consistency conditioned on geometry.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建 GeoFlip，一个以几何干预引发物理结果翻转的视频生成基准：固定物理设置与文本提示，仅改变支撑范围、物体位置和机构配置，形成 482 组配对场景与 964 段参考视频，并对 16 个图像到视频模型在事件正确性、结构完整性与参考相似度上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 配对干预可核查模型是否真正使用首帧几何证据、还是被先验或文本旁路主导，与 LVR 中视觉信息保留和证据筛选的诊断思路相通；但它是视频生成基准，能否迁移为 latent 推理状态的评价工具尚待核查。
